Uncertainty, not a finding. (1) Dedupe keeps the first occurrence per id. Oracle fixtures reuse the same object per id across days, so the oracle cannot tell which day record wins. No promise (E1 to E5) names record fields, so no gap is recorded. (2) Team and Portfolio loop: buildViewData receives ownerKind but the four over-time lists have no owner-dependent branch, so the owner dimension does not discriminate. Acceptable against E1 to E5. (3) E5 reload is modelled as a second pure buildViewData call on a second RunChartData; no stateful reload is exercised. Acceptable for a pure list builder. (4) Throughput, arrivals and started-and-closed lists now also deduplicate via extractWorkItems (widgetViewData.ts lines 88 to 113). Their items arrive or close once, so one row per item is the correct reading; no new oracle, per root scope; existing selected tests pass (415).
